rationale: The workflow already implements several evidence-supported optimizations: (1) Path filtering via paths-ignore on both push and pull_request triggers (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER), (2) uv dependency caching via astral-sh/setup-uv@v4 with enable-cache: true and cache-dependency-glob (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE / P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE), (3) Matrix testing across Python versions. The remaining patterns either require reducing test coverage (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST would skip remaining Python versions on first failure, contrary to 'preserve intended test coverage'), need historical runtime data not available (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT), or apply to scheduled/queued workflows not present here (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE, P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY). The P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE experiment shows ~9% savings but for a pip-based workflow without uv caching; this workflow's uv caching already addresses dependency download reuse. No supported optimization improves this workflow without trade-offs or missing prerequisites.
